name: LoveDA: Land-Cover Domain Adaptive Semantic Segmentation Dataset
description: LoveDA is a high-spatial-resolution remote sensing land-cover dataset constructed by the RSIDEA research group at Wuhan University. Designed to benchmark semantic segmentation and domain adaptation algorithms across varying geographical distributions, LoveDA contains 5,987 images of 1024x1024 pixels at 0.3-meter ground resolution, featuring 166,768 annotated objects across 7 categories (background, building, road, water, barren, forest, agricultural). The dataset captures stark domain shifts between dense urban (2,713 images) and sparse rural (3,274 images) landscapes across three Chinese cities (Nanjing, Changzhou, and Wuhan). The standard benchmark partition comprises 2,522 training images, 1,669 validation images, and 1,796 held-out test images.

size.notes: 5,987 1024x1024 RGB TIFF images paired with PNG semantic segmentation masks. Standard evaluation split: 2,522 train, 1,669 val, 1,796 test; domain distribution: 2,713 urban, 3,274 rural.

provenance.collection_method: Extracted from Google Earth high-resolution imagery covering 18 rural and urban areas in Nanjing, Changzhou, and Wuhan.
provenance.curation_notes: Pixel-level annotation for 7 categories performed with cross-validation. Explicitly distinguishes urban from rural distributions for unsupervised domain adaptation benchmarking.
